newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus will not charge officers for mob shootings.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus will not charge officers for mob shootings.

text.p: Cyprus's attorney general on Wednesday said that due to lack of evidence no action will be taken against policemen suspected of involvement in mob shootings last year.
Alecos Markides announced the decision after almost a year of inquiries into allegations senior police officers were behind a murder and a murder attempt last year.

"I have exhausted a study of the matter... and reached the conclusion that based on the information gathered and legal arguments in mind, filing for prosecution is not the indicated route," Markides told a news conference.
A gambling club owner was shot dead on the steps of his establishment last year by unknown assailants in Limassol, a sprawling town on the island's southern coast and site of many unsolved crimes.
A month earlier his nephew was shot and critically wounded in what police described as a turf war between different gangs at the time.
Later, allegations of police involvement surfaced after political party leaders were summoned to the presidential palace for an off-the-record briefing on crime.
A few days later Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides publicly admitted police officers were suspected of involvement in organised crime.

The accusations stemmed from an alleged recorded confession by one of the police officers to his superior officer. In a subsequent conversation, also recorded, the same officer retracted his earlier confession, Markides said.
"These cases will not close because at any moment new evidence may be discovered, a witness who was too scared to talk may talk," said Markides. "They are considered open."
